outcome.technical: _floor_guard.py: a fourth answer, PARTLY_READ; each notRead entry carries kind (could-hold-one or cannot-hold-a-move); binary files are listed before the no-hunk return; a deleted+added pair of one family at git's similarity is read as a rename (RENAME_SIMILARITY) and a test moved unchanged across files is not gone; skip and stub kind-pairing only on the two sides of one changed line or in one enclosing scope; class head and decorators, pytestmark and if/with/try heads are part of each test's comparison, with skip reasons blanked in a parse-time pass (keeps the recursion depth of HEAD); labelled-check suites compared by label; outside code: additions count as compared, base statements gone or changed, or an added return/raise/break/continue in a base function, make the file could-hold; bare-path declarations cover only new definitions; suppression markers anchored per kind (_MARKER_AT); a non-Python test file matching no assertion row is could-hold. _filed_returns.py: FLOOR_ANSWERS gains partly-read, kinds, floor_unread_kind/floor_not_compared/floor_verdict, the summary is bounded (clean counts recorded prose and names no basis), floor_lines says NOT clean overall only for could-hold files, and floor_block refuses a block whose entry or base is not an object (it used to raise in the readers). drive-phase.py: floor_diff detects renames in the tracked diff; floor_declared docstring. _status_facts.py: kinds from floor_verdict, a fifth list declared. audit-status.py: declared line, id list cut between ids with 'and N more'. Docs: README, execute-task.md, phase-signoff.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG. Suites: test__floor_guard 98/98, test__filed_returns 139/139, test__status_facts 199/199, test_audit_status 420/420, drive flm-block 5/5; final six-suite sweep 6/6 files, 2065 cases, exit 0. Mutations (scratchpad sg1.19/mutations.py, throwaway copy, anchors asserted once, pycache purged and restore checked per row): 36 rows, every one KILLED, deny and allow per item and per half of the added paragraph. Measurement (sg1.19/measure.py, 1023 task commits, before = HEAD guard with --no-renames, after = edited guard with renames): before clean 2, declared 0, partly-read 928, findings 93; after clean 462, declared 1, partly-read 269, findings 291. Every partly-read commit after, with file and reason: sg1.19/partly_read_after.txt (384 file entries: 307 'code outside its labelled checks changed', 77 'code outside its test definitions changed'). Findings grew because row suites are now compared: 198 commits moved partly-read -> findings, all definition-changed; of the 1030 definition-changed findings after, 411 sit in the task's own tests.add file (a bare path no longer covers an existing case) and 619 in files the task did not declare. Old blocks (sg1.19/old_blocks.py): all 16 filed blocks read through floor_summary and floor_lines with HEAD's and the edited reader, none raise, and the only diff is prose files leaving the 'not compared' count. Probes 1-4 rerun after: all exit 0, outputs in sg1.19/after/. The orchestrator's live_mine.py: FAILS: 0, and no expectation in it is wrong. Shape changed_rels hands floor_diff: two separate entries (rel, rel, untracked). For git mv both are tracked (False), and the tracked diff now carries 'rename from/rename to'. For a plain move the new path is untracked (True) and is diffed against /dev/null, so the guard pairs the deletion with the addition. Untrue against the code: (1) 'every existing case stays green' conflicts with items 4 and 5 and the added paragraph; the HEAD versions of fa3, fa4, fa12, fa14 and fa19 in tests/test__floor_guard.py, fl1 and fl7 in tests/test__status_facts.py, and ffg1 in tests/test__filed_returns.py pinned the old behaviour and were changed to the new rule. (2) plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md (around line 277 at HEAD) named the field cannotTell; the block's field is couldNotTell (fixed). (3) gitleaks and semgrep read their markers anywhere on a code line, so the reviewer's prose rows for them were honest only on comment-only lines. One plan-gate refusal, met while editing my own scratch script: '[plan gate] A source-file write from a heredoc fed to an interpreter's stdin (python3 - <<EOF ...), which is the same capability as python -c and is graded as one bypasses the plan-first gate: mutations.py (in the linked worktree ...)'. The same edit was then made with the Edit tool, which the gate allowed. No tools/prove-gates.py row is owed: no _violations, _drift or _claims name was added, and the existing plain_read_violations already has its rows.
outcome.descriptive: The floor guard answers clean only for what it compared: unread files that could hold a move make the answer partly read, prose and data do not, moved tests are no deletions, and row suites are compared check by check.
